metadata.title: Development of a Shared System REMS (draft guidance for industry)
metadata.legal_basis: FDA draft guidance under FD&C Act section 505-1(i).
metadata.applicability: ANDA applicants and reference-product holders developing a single, shared system REMS.

candidates.context: This guidance provides recommendations to industry on the development of a shared system risk 15 evaluation and mitigation strategy (REMS) 2 for multiple prescription drug (including biological) 16 products. 3 This guidance describes some of the possible benefits of a shared system REMS, and 17 provides general principles and recommendations to assist industry with the development of 18 these programs. This guidance does not discuss the process for requesting a waiver of the single, 19 shared system REMS requirement that applies to abbreviated new drug applications (ANDAs) 20 referencing a listed drug with an approved REMS. 4 FDA issued a separate guidance describing 21 the process for requesting waivers and the criteria FDA applies in considering them. 5 1 This guidance has been prepared by the Office of Surveillance and Epidemiology, Office of New Drugs, Office of Generic Drugs, and Of

candidates.context: The Food and Drug Administration Amendments Act of 2007 (FDAAA) 6 created section 505-1 35 of the FD&C Act, which authorizes FDA to require a REMS if FDA determines that a REMS is 36 necessary to ensure that the benefits of the drug outweigh its risks. 7 A REMS is a required risk 37 management strategy that employs tools beyond prescribing information to ensure that the 38 benefits of a drug outweigh its risks. candidates.statement: Additionally, FDA may request that applicants for a class of products with a similar risk profile 118 develop a shared system REMS. Applicants that are interested in developing a shared system 119 REMS for a class of products should seek the advice of FDA. 19
candidates.context: For example, we recommend the applicants for a product submitted under section 505(b)(2) of 111 the FD&C Act or section 351(k) of the PHS Act work together with the applicant for the product 112 they are referencing to establish a shared system REMS. If an applicant of a product submitted 113 under section 505(b)(2) of the FD&C Act or section 351(k) of the PHS Act seeks to develop a 114 shared system REMS, we encourage the applicant to contact the applicant of the product they are 115 referencing and begin joint development of the shared system REMS as early as possible. 116 III. DEVELOPING A SHARED SYSTEM REMS PROGRAM 123

candidates.statement: Applicants may consider forming a working group, commonly referred to as an industry working 152 group (IWG). Some applicants have used an IWG to facilitate negotiations and agreements 153 among the applicants to develop a shared system REMS on issues such as confidentiality, 154 governance, voting structure, cost-sharing, any potential changes to the drug distribution model, 155 and any other issues that may come up during the collaboration. Some applicants have used 156 third-party vendors to aid in implementation and management of the program. The applicants 157 must comply with the requirements of the REMS regardless of whether they use a third-party 158 vendor. 159
candidates.context: B. Formation of an Industry Working Group 150 If an IWG is formed, the IWG applicants should identify a single point of contact (POC) to 161 represent the IWG in communication with FDA. This POC will facilitate communication 162 between the Agency and the IWG about the status of developing the shared system. FDA 163 generally requests that the Agency receive updates from the IWG POC on the status of 164 negotiations and on any barriers to developing the shared system REMS based on timelines that 165 have been communicated by the Agency early in the process. The updates are typically 166 submitted to each respective application as a REMS correspondence. 167

candidates.statement: Information about the performance of REMS programs is important in determining whether the 186 program is meeting its intended risk mitigation goals. All approved REMS for NDA and BLA 187 products are required to include a timetable for submission of assessments of the REMS. 23 The 188 proposed REMS assessment plan for a shared system REMS, which specifies the nature and 189 content of the periodic assessments, is generally included in the REMS supporting document. 190
candidates.context: IV. SHARED SYSTEM REMS ASSESSMENTS 184 The assessments for shared system REMS apply collectively to all products that are subject to 192 the REMS. The Agency generally does not require submission of the shared REMS assessment 193 reports for ANDAs that are part of a shared system REMS with an RLD. However, FDA may 194 require that ANDA applicants submit REMS assessment reports when product-specific 195 utilization information or adverse event data is necessary to evaluate whether the program should 196 be modified to ensure the benefits of the drug outweigh the risks or to minimize the burden on 197 the health care delivery system of complying with the REMS. 24

candidates.statement: Applicants that are developing a shared system REMS should submit their REMS by application 232 midpoint for pending applications, or another time frame specified by the Agency. To facilitate 233 submission tracking, FDA recommends that shared system REMS applicants work together to 234 coordinate their submissions on the same day, if possible. 235

candidates.statement: If applicants that are participating in a shared system REMS choose to use a DMF, they should refer to the draft guidance for industry Use of a Drug Master File for Shared System REMS Submissions . 33 Additional, and more-detailed, submission instructions are also included in a separate technical guide. 34
candidates.context: To improve the efficiency of the submission and review process for shared system REMS, FDA 262 recommends that applicants use a Type V 32 Drug Master File (DMF) for their shared system 263 REMS submissions. Using a DMF allows applicants that are part of a shared system REMS to 264 submit one set of files on behalf of the application holders to the Agency and eliminates the need 265 for each applicant to submit identical REMS-related documents to its own application. The DMF 266 holder of the shared systems REMS DMF is jointly designated by the application holders. The 267 DMF holder will make submissions to the DMF on behalf of the application holders. 268 30 There may also be instances where the approval of a shared system REMS between multiple NDAs may coincide with one or more NDAs receiving tentative approval.
